explanation: The March 20, 2019 document contains substantive content including a formal announcement of balance sheet runoff cessation and transition to an 'ample reserves' regime, a notably dovish shift in the economic outlook (GDP 'slowed markedly' in Q1, inflation 'declined'), and the SEP/dot plot signaling zero rate hikes in 2019—all of which would plausibly drive a structural break in rates and equity markets around March 7 as pre-meeting communications and data releases (e.g., the weak February payrolls report on March 8) telegraphed this dovish pivot. The January 30 document also contributed by introducing the 'patient' forward guidance framework, but the March meeting crystallized the full dovish regime shift.
